# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to

The harness doc says: "Use this when the assertion contract is the SCREEN" — so the change from `waitForText` → `waitForScreen` for `_olderRow` aligns with the harness's guidance.

Now let me think about the timing analysis carefully — the core of this fix:

Timeline of the first scenario (per column width):
1. Boot: `waitForBoot()` — banner `[Model]` + settle.
2. Wave one turn: `sendText('run wave one')` + Enter. The scripted stream emits 'launching the first wave' text + 5 tool calls (sleep 21..25, background). Wait for `Background jobs (5)` on screen (60s timeout). Wait for `_replyOne` (60s). `waitForOutput(settleMs: 400)`.
3. Wave two turn: `sendText('run wave two')` + Enter. Text + 6 tool calls (sleep 300, background). Wait for `_olderRow` via `waitForScreen` (60s). `waitForOutput(settleMs: 400)`. Capture `before`.
4. Freeze proof: `beforeOlder` must have exactly 1 row `· older` and `(5)`.
5. `waitForText(_firstSettle)` (60s) — first `exited(0)` at ~21s after wave-one job launch.
6. mid capture: `· older` row must equal `beforeOlder`.
7. `waitForText(_settledCardBody)` (60s) — full settle at ~25s.
8. after capture: aged row gone, exactly one settled card, wave two stays live.
9. `/exit`, wait exit code.

Total wall time per iteration: boot (~2-10s) + wave one (~2-5s) + wave two (~2-5s) + wait until first settle (the remaining of 21s since wave-one launch, minus elapsed) + up to 4s to last settle + settle buffers + exit. If boot+turns take ~10s, iteration ≈ 30-35s. Three iterations ≈ 100-105s, plus scenario B. Well within the 10-minute `@Timeout`.

Key race analysis:
- Old: sleeps 5..9s from wave-one launch. The `before` capture happens after wave-two's board row appears. On a slow runner, boot (~5s) + turn 1 (~3s) + turn 2 (~2s) + turn 3 (~3s) ≈ 13s > 9s — the entire wave-one bucket could be fully settled and drained by the time `before` is captured. Then `beforeOlder` is empty → `Expected: an object with length of <1> / Actual: []`. Matches the CI signature exactly. New: base 20 → settles at 21..25s, comfortably after the ~10s worst-case capture. Margin ~11s+. 

- Is 21..25s enough margin? Worst-case runner latency claim: boot + two scripted turns + PTY polling ≈ 10 s on fa-m5 minis. The `before` capture requires wave-two board row painted; if boot+3 turns took >21s, the capture would again miss. But the PR description says ~10s worst observed; 21 gives ~2x margin. Reasonable.

- One subtle thing: `_firstSettle` timeout raised 30→60s: the first settle lands at ~21s after wave-one launch; at the `waitForText(_firstSettle)` call, maybe ~10-15s have elapsed, so remaining ~6-11s normally; 30s would be plenty. But on a very slow runner, boot+turns could take longer... the deadline starts at the wait call; the settle happens 21s after launch regardless. If boot+turns took 15s, remaining wait = 6s. 30s was fine; 60s just absorbs extreme lag where the first settle could fire... hmm, actually the wait can't exceed ~21s after wave-one launch. If boot+turns took <21s, remaining wait <21s. If boot+turns took >21s, the bucket is already drained before `before` capture → the earlier `beforeOlder` assertion fails first. So the 30→60s raise is defensive, harmless.

- `_settledCardBody` timeout 30→60s: full settle at ~25s after launch; call happens at ~21s; remaining ~4s normally; if the runner is slow (say 15s to capture), remaining 10s. 30s was probably fine, 60s defensive. Harmless.

Potential concerns to flag in review:

1. **Test duration/timeout budget**: sleeps raised 5..9 → 21..25 nearly doubles per-iteration wall time (~+16s × 3 widths ≈ +48s). With the 10-minute file `@Timeout`, still fine. But CI job timeouts at the workflow level? Let me check how integration tests run in CI — the `--tags integration` suite. If there's a per-shard timeout, +48s could matter. Let me check `.github/workflows`.

2. **`waitForScreen` vs raw-text for `_olderRow`**: The regex `r'Background jobs \(5\) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older'` — in `screenText`, lines are joined and trimmed of empty lines. `waitForScreen` checks `screen.contains(pattern)`. The viewport line may have the `· older` suffix... the row is painted as one line if wide enough; at 80 columns, could `Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older` wrap or elide? The row is the collapsed board summary row. At 80 columns: "┌─ Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older …" — hmm, that's ~60+ chars plus border. `┌─ ` (3) + text (~55) + maybe more. The test previously used `waitForText` with the same regex and passed on main (the ticket says main is green on this file, and this exact test at 80 cols passed — the failing case was the timing race, not the match). So the row fits at 80 cols. OK.

   Actually wait — careful: `waitForScreen` checks `screenText` which strips empty lines and joins — the row might be split across two physical lines if wrapped. But since main passed with the same regex on screen (the frame in the ticket shows `┌─ Background jobs (5) · 0 running · 5 done · 0 lost` — hmm that's from the failing capture; the actual older-row format `· 5 running · 0 done`), it fits. Also `Terminal(maxLines: rows * 4)` — viewport fine.

3. **A deeper design question**: the fix keeps the assertion `expect(beforeOlder, hasLength(1))` dependent on timing margin (21s vs ~10s). It's a mitigation, not an elimination of the race. A more robust approach: instead of relying on sleeps outlasting runner latency, gate the `before` capture on the board state itself (e.g. wait for the screen to show `5 running · 0 done` for wave one's older row). Actually — `waitForScreen(_olderRow)` already waits for exactly `Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older` — which is only true while ALL FIVE wave-one jobs are still running (5 running · 0 done). So the `before` capture now requires the row in its all-running state. If a job had settled early, the row would read `4 running · 1 done` and `waitForScreen(_olderRow)` would time out rather than silently passing... wait, would it? The frozen-row semantics: the printed `· older` row is a frozen snapshot — it prints `5 running · 0 done` when the bucket ages out (moves to `older`) and never re-derives. The aging out happens when a NEWER bucket takes the live slot (wave two's launch). So `_olderRow` = the frozen snapshot with `5 running · 0 done`. If a wave-one job settles BEFORE wave two launches, then at aging time the snapshot would read `4 running · 1 done` (or the bucket may have drained entirely) → `_olderRow` never appears → `waitForScreen` times out after 60s → test fails with a clear timeout instead of the confusing `[]` assertion. So the new gating makes the failure mode explicit and diagnostic. Good.

When wave two lands, wave one's row ages to `· older` frozen at... the counts at aging time = `4 running · 1 done`? Then `_olderRow` (5 running · 0 done · older) wouldn't match → timeout. On slow runners (boot+turns > 21s), this could still occur... at 21s base with ~10s worst, fine. So the residual race is: capture must happen within ~11s of margin. OK.

# self-skip those legs gracefully; the gate stays honest either way.
      # coverage-gardener that bumps the baseline: the live-provider legs
      # (unlocked by these keys) load extra lib/src/cli surface into the
      # measurement, so a no-key run measures a DIFFERENT — higher —
      # number and would pass while the nightly fails. Missing keys (forks)
      # self-skip those legs gracefully; the gate stays honest either way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
      # Self-hosted fa-m5 minis have no /Users/runner home — setup-* would
      # try to mkdir the hosted toolcache and die. Redirect it to a stable
      # per-runner path (warm across runs); hosted runners are untouched.
      - name: Self-hosted toolcache redirect (fa-m5)
        if: startsWith(runner.name, 'fa-m5')
        run: echo "RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE=${{ runner.workspace }}/toolcache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # setup-python hardcodes AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY=/Users/runner/hostedtoolcache
      # on every macOS runner (hosted layout assumption) and overwrites
      # RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE, so on self-hosted macs without a 'runner' user it
      # dies with "mkdir: /Users/runner: Permission denied". The only python
      # consumer here is the pure-python coverage ratchet below — system
      # python3 (CLT on macOS, preinstalled on hosted images) suffices.
      - name: python3 available
        run: python3 --version
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: dart test --tags integration (excluding browser-ext)
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
          --coverage=coverage
      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
      - name: CLI coverage ratchet (lib/src/cli/**, baseline only up)
        run: python3 scripts/check_cli_coverage.py

blocks.text:
The integration leg (`dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext --coverage=coverage`) has a 60-minute job timeout (line 500's `timeout-minutes: 60` corresponds to the job containing line 550). Adding ~30-50s to one file within a 60-minute leg is negligible. The file-level `@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 10))` comfortably absorbs the +30-50s.

Now, let me validate the test compiles and analyzer is clean, and quickly run the non-PTY unit test the PR description references (`test/cli/shell_job_board_test.dart`, 35 tests) as sanity. Also try to run the changed integration test? It's a real PTY test, spawning the CLI with scripted streams; it could take ~2-3 min. It would be strong verification. The environment is a Linux runner with dart available? Let me check `dart --version`. The repo has pubspec; tests may need `dart pub get`. Let me try analyzer first.

Also, let me double check one potential correctness subtlety: at 80 columns, does the frozen row fit so `waitForScreen` can match `Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older` as one screen line? screenLines drops empty lines and keeps others; contains() on the joined text — if the row wrapped into two lines, the joined string would contain a `\n` in the middle → no match → 60s timeout → flaky. But: main is green with `waitForText` which ALSO checks screenText (`output.contains(pattern) || screenText.contains(pattern)`) — and the row appears in the failing CI frame as a single line `┌─ Background jobs (5) · 0 running · 5 done · 0 lost`. The full string with `· 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older`: "Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older" is 57 chars; plus "┌─ " prefix = 60 chars; fits 80 cols. The `_olderRow` regex is matched against screenText (which joins lines with \n) — fits one line. OK.

Another subtlety: `viewportLines` at 80x24 — `Terminal(maxLines: rows * 4)`. Fine.

One more: the PR bumps `_firstSettle`/`_settledCardBody` timeouts 30→60s "to absorb slow-runner render/persist lag past the longer sleeps". Since the file has @Timeout(10 min), a hung wait would still terminate. Fine.

Now, is there any ISSUE with the increase? Let me think about the whole-suite duration math precisely.

Per width iteration:
- boot: waitForBoot (up to 90s timeout; typical 2-8s)
- wave one turn: ~1-3s (scripted, instant)
- wait `Background jobs (5)`: instant-ish after board paints
- wait `_replyOne`: turn 2 scripted, ~1s
- settle 400ms
- wave two turn: ~1-3s
- waitForScreen(_olderRow): instant after wave-two board paints (~1-2s)
- settle 400ms
- capture `before` at T ≈ boot + ~6-10s
- wave-one jobs settle at 21-25s after their launch (which happened during turn 1, ~2-4s after boot). So first settle at wall ~23-29s; wait for it ≈ 13-19s.
- mid capture, then wait full settle (last at ~25s after launch → ~29s wall; ~2-8s more).
- `after` capture, assertions, `/exit` + exit-code wait (15s cap).

So per iteration ≈ 35-45s (vs ~20-25s before) → +~50s total across 3 widths. Test 2 (restart) also launches wave one with the longer sleeps, but kills before settle; duration unchanged (~boot + a few seconds).

Everything fits: file timeout 10 min; CI leg 60 min. Good.

Now the deeper review question — does this fix actually address the root cause robustly, or just widen the race window? The failure was: whole bucket settled+drained before `before` capture → `beforeOlder` empty. The fix: (a) push the settle window 2.3x further out (21..25s vs worst ~10s capture latency), and (b) gate the capture on the screen showing the frozen all-running row (`waitForScreen(_olderRow)` — `5 running · 0 done`), so if the bucket did drain early, the test now fails with a 60s timeout naming the pattern + screen dump (a diagnosable failure), not a confusing empty-list assertion. Combined, this converts both the likely case (never happens with 2x margin) and the residual case (clear diagnostic) into better states. That's a sound mitigation for a test-only flake.

Residual nit: the ~2x margin is empirical ("~10 s worst on fa-m5-class runners"), not enforced — a runner 2x slower than the observed worst would reintroduce the empty-capture failure, but now with the timeout diagnostic (b). Acceptable; could note as SUGGESTION-level: consider making the margin structural, e.g., waiting for the first wave-one settle to be IMMINENT before capturing... actually you can't easily assert "not yet settled" other than what waitForScreen(_olderRow) already does (the frozen row only exists while the newer bucket is live AND prints all-running counts — hmm, actually the frozen row is printed at aging time with then-current counts; if the bucket ages at `5 running · 0 done` the row is exactly `_olderRow`. waitForScreen returns as soon as that row is painted. A wave-one job can't settle before aging unless latency > 21s. So (b) already structuralizes the capture: the capture happens strictly before any settle, unless the 21s window is exceeded, in which case timeout — not a false pass. That IS the structural fix; the base=20 just needs to stay above realistic latency. Good.)

One more consideration — false-pass risk introduced by waitForScreen for `_olderRow`: previously waitForText matched raw OR screen. Raw matching could fire on the row's raw bytes before painted... now screen-only, strictly stronger. No false-pass introduced.

What about `_firstSettle = 'exited(0)'` — `waitForText` matches raw OR screen. The raw stream includes the settle notice printed by the CLI (`[bash] sh-… exited(0)`). This is a transcript notice — fine. But could 'exited(0)' appear EARLY from something else? The `/exit` command? No — that's later. Wave-two jobs sleep 300s. OK, unchanged behavior anyway.

Now check: are there other tests/files that copy the same wave pattern with 4+i sleeps that would also need the fix? The ticket is specific to this test. Quick grep for 'p539-wave1' or 'sleep ${4' to check duplication.

Also verify the claim "Both tests pass" — I'll try to run the changed integration test if the environment allows (needs dart + pub get + pty + bash `sleep`). It runs `dart bin/fah.dart`... spawns real CLI with FA_TEST_STREAM_SCRIPT. Should work on Linux runner. Time: ~2-4 min. Worth it for a high-confidence review. But careful: it writes to /tmp/fa_539_home and /tmp/fa_539_proj (shared fixed paths) — fine solo.

`shell_job_board_test.dart`: 35/35 green — matches the PR description's claim.

Now while the integration test runs, let me do the remaining review due diligence:

1. Impact analysis (grep fallback for CodeGraph): the changed file is a test; consumers = CI workflow only. Checked.

2. Check the `_firstSettle`/`_settledCardBody` raise and `waitForScreen` change against sibling PTY tests using `waitForScreen` — established pattern (harness doc references #550/#557 flake family). Let me quickly grep how many tests use waitForScreen to confirm it's an established convention.

3. Re-read the final changed file for the exhaustive pass — done above; findings so far:
   - SUGGESTION: the two 60s timeout raises + `_olderRow` 60s — could share a named const (e.g. `_settleWindowTimeout`), but the file consistently uses inline durations; not worth blocking.
   - SUGGESTION: comment says "~10 s worst on fa-m5-class runners" — the margin (21 vs 10) is empirical; the residual failure mode is now a diagnosable 60s timeout (acceptable; maybe mention as observation, not even a suggestion).
   - POSSIBLE IMPORTANT/BLOCKING? Let me think hard about anything that could actually bite:
     a. Scenario B now launches wave one with sleeps 21..25 and hard-kills after `Background jobs (5)` + 600ms — kill happens well before any settle (21s) → `5 background tasks lost` stable. Actually IMPROVED determinism (before, on a very slow boot, a job could have settled pre-kill and broken the count). Positive side effect worth mentioning in general comment.
     b. Test wall-time: +~40-60s total; within file 10-min and CI leg 60-min budgets. Verified above.
     c. `waitForScreen` semantics — verified in harness; used correctly; returns screen not raw, return value discarded here — fine.
     d. The `before` capture's race window is now structurally closed by `_olderRow`'s `5 running · 0 done` gating (capture can only happen when all five jobs still live and bucket aged-out-but-frozen). Solid.
     e. Any issue with `_waveOneSleepBase = 20` naming vs comment "Wave one's first sleep (seconds): its jobs settle at base+1 .. base+5" — accurate (sleep = base+i, i=1..5).
     f. Ticket reconciliation: ticket asserted a product regression in ai/gh-869 and demanded a product fix; this PR demonstrates (byte-identical lib/bin/test between main and the branch) it was test timing, and fixes the test on main so #899 can re-run. The PR description argues this well. From the repo's perspective: the branch ai/gh-937 ALSO contains a merge of origin/main (6a28ce46) — the diff vs main is exactly the test change. Scope-clean.
     g. Security: nothing — test-only, no secrets, commands are `sleep N && echo`. The `/tmp/fa_539_*` fixed paths are pre-existing (and #936 handles hub hygiene). No new risk. Note: setUp doesn't delete pre-existing /tmp/fa_539_home contents, but pre-existing behavior, unchanged by this PR.
     h. Backward compat: test-only. n/a.
     i. Dead code/unused imports: none added.
   
4. One more possible flag: the doc comment on `_waveOneSleepBase` says "staggered ~1 s apart. The base keeps every job alive well past boot + two scripted turns + harness polling (~10 s worst…)" — "two scripted turns" — after turn 1 (launch), turns 2 and 3 precede the capture: that's two MORE turns. Accurate.

5. Also should confirm the changed file's diff numbers used for inline comments correspond to the PR diff's right-hand side. Computed: 40, 55, 218, 236, 254 — all within hunks (31-44, 52-58, 213-221, 233-239, 251-257). 

Let me also quickly double-check that line 218 is `await harness.waitForScreen(` — grep showed `218:      await harness.waitForScreen(`. Yes.

And line 236 / 254 are the two raised timeouts (the `timeout:` lines). In the diff, hunk `@@ -223,7 +233,7 @@`: new lines 233-239:
233: `expect(beforeOlder, hasLength(1), ...` — wait let me recount. Actually hunk header `@@ -223,7 +233,7 @@` means new side starts at 233 with 7 lines. Lines:
233: (context) `      expect(beforeOlder, hasLength(1), reason: 'frame before:\n$before');` hmm...

Let me just recompute from the actual file to be safe. From grep: 236 is `timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),` for _firstSettle; 254 for _settledCardBody. Both are "+"-lines in the diff (changed from 30). Good.

Line 55 is the sleep line — "+" line. Line 40 — the const. Hmm wait, line 40 is `const int _waveOneSleepBase = 20;`? grep says 40. And the doc comment lines 34-39ish. The `+` added block in diff hunk 1: new lines 34-39 are the doc comment (6 lines: /// Wave one's first sleep... (gh-937).) then line 40 `const int _waveOneSleepBase = 20;`. Wait — the hunk `@@ -31,6 +31,14 @@`: new lines 31-44. Added lines (6 of them: 5 doc lines + const? the diff shows 7 added lines actually: `+/// Wave one's first sleep (seconds): its jobs settle at base+1 .. base+5,` ... let me count: the diff adds:

```
+/// Wave one's first sleep (seconds): its jobs settle at base+1 .. base+5,
+/// staggered ~1 s apart. The base keeps every job alive well past boot +
+/// two scripted turns + harness polling (~10 s worst on fa-m5-class
+/// runners) — with the original 5..9 s window the whole bucket could
+/// settle and drain BEFORE the freeze proof's `before` capture, leaving
+/// no frozen `· older` row to assert on (gh-937).
+const int _waveOneSleepBase = 20;
```
7 added lines (+15 total: 7 here + 3 comment lines around waitForScreen (2 added + 1 changed→ counts as +1 net... let me not over-count; git says +15/-5). 15 = 7 (doc+const) + 1 (sleep line changed counts as +1) + 2 (waitForScreen comment) + 1 (waitForScreen line) + 1 (settle comment line) + 1 (firstSettle timeout) + 1 (settledCardBody timeout) = 14. Hmm, one more: the `// The screen is the assertion contract...` is 2 lines. 7+1+2+1+1+1+1 = 14. Diff stat says 15 insertions. Whatever — the pr_files stat says +15/-5; the actual git diff origin/main...HEAD gives the same 15/5. Close enough; counting by hand is error-prone.

So for inline comments:
- Comment on line 40 (the const + doc) — the timing-margin design; SUGGESTION or just positive note? I'd make one comment about the residual-race/measurement: classify as SUGGESTION (optional: consider asserting the margin structurally or naming the constant's relationship to a measured budget). Hmm — actually waitForScreen already structuralizes it. The remaining suggestion: the empirical "~10 s worst" has no enforcement; if runner latency regresses 2x, the suite degrades to a 60s-timeout failure (diagnosable). That's fine. I could keep this as an observation in general.md instead of an inline comment.

- Comment on line 218 (waitForScreen) — positive/IMPORTANT? It's the correct harness idiom per its own doc (#550/#557). No issue. Maybe no comment needed.

- Comment on lines 236/254 (60s raises) — SUGGESTION: consider a shared named constant for the settle-window timeout since four call sites now use `Duration(seconds: 60)` in this test (also 205, 209 for the wave turns, 307 in scenario B). Minor. Actually 205/209/307 are pre-existing 60s. So the new raises just join the existing convention. This is a very weak suggestion. Hmm.

- A more valuable comment: test duration cost. The sleep base raise adds ~30-50s to every CI run of this suite (3 geometries × ~16s). Within budgets (file 10 min, leg 60 min) — verified. So not even IMPORTANT. Maybe mention in general.md.

## PR #940 (gh-937) — Review Verdict: ✅ APPROVE

**The change**: +15/−5 in `test/integration/job_board_stability_pty_test.dart` only — wave-one sleeps raised 5→9s → 21→25s (`_waveOneSleepBase = 20`), the aged-row wait moved from `waitForText` to `waitForScreen`, and two downstream waits 30s→60s. No product code touched.

**Verification performed (all claims confirmed locally)**:
- `dart analyze` on the changed file + harness: **clean**
- `dart test/cli/shell_job_board_test.dart`: **35/35 pass**
- `dart test --tags integration test/integration/job_board_stability_pty_test.dart`: **2/2 pass** — including the previously deterministically-red stacked-boards case

**Key findings**:
1. **No blocking/important issues.** The load-bearing fix is actually the `waitForScreen(_olderRow)` gate: the frozen `· older` row only ever reads `5 running · 0 done` while all five jobs are live, so an overrun of the 20s base now fails as a diagnosable 60s timeout with a screen dump — not the old silent `Expected: length <1> / Actual: []`.
2. **The "no product regression" claim is substantiated by repo evidence**: `git diff origin/main...HEAD` = this test file only; the #899 merge content (`a607f1e7`) touches only `flutter_app/` + `packages/fa_ui/`, which the CLI PTY suite never loads. The ticket's product-regression A/B conclusion was wrong — the `5 done · 0 lost` CI signature is exactly the drain-before-capture race this PR reproduces and fixes.
3. **Positive side effect**: scenario B's `hardKill()` now always precedes the first settle, making the `5 background tasks lost` count race-free too.
4. **CI budget impact**: +~16s × 3 geometries ≈ +50s/run — well within the file's 10-min `@Timeout` and the integration leg's 60-min job timeout.

**Suggestions (2, non-blocking)**: document the measured ~10s capture-latency budget next to `_waveOneSleepBase` (comment1, line 40); deduplicate the six now-identical `Duration(seconds: 60)` literals (comment2, line 236). Both anchor lines verified present in the diff hunks.

**Next steps for the author**: merge, re-dispatch CI on `ai/gh-869` before unblocking #899, and update ticket gh-937's conclusion (product regression → test-timing race).

## PR Description

### What changed
Fixed the deterministic `job_board_stability_pty_test` red on PR #899 (ai/gh-869): the freeze-proof's `before` capture now has a settle window (wave-one sleeps 21..25 s, was 5..9 s) that outlasts worst-case runner latency (boot + two scripted turns + PTY polling ≈ 10 s on fa-m5 minis), and the aged-row wait binds to the painted screen (`waitForScreen`) instead of the raw byte stream.

### Key decisions
- **No product change** — `lib/`, `bin/` and `test/` are byte-identical between `main` and `ai/gh-869` (only `flutter_app/`+`packages/fa_ui` differ, unused by the CLI), so a product regression was impossible; the A/B conclusion in the ticket was a test-timing race, not a composer/status-row bug.
- Reproduced the exact CI signature (`Expected: an object with length of <1> / Actual: []` at line 223, frame showing `┌─ Background jobs (5) · 0 running · 5 done · 0 lost`) by compressing the settle window: the whole bucket legitimately settled and drained before the capture — freeze + drain-once behaved correctly.
- Kept the ~1 s settle stagger the between-settles freeze assertion requires; `_firstSettle`/`_settledCardBody` timeouts raised 30 s → 60 s to absorb slow-runner render/persist lag past the longer sleeps.
- To un-block #899: merge `ai/gh-937` (or cherry-pick `2a70f077`) into `ai/gh-869`, then re-dispatch CI. #899 must not be admin-merged before that.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test --tags integration test/integration/job_board_stability_pty_test.dart
```
Both tests pass (was: deterministic failure of the 80/120/200 stacked-boards case on slow runners); `dart test test/cli/shell_job_board_test.dart` 35/35 green; analyzer clean.

## PR Description

### What changed
Fixed the deterministic `job_board_stability_pty_test` red on PR #899 (ai/gh-869): the freeze-proof's `before` capture now has a settle window (wave-one sleeps 21..25 s, was 5..9 s) that outlasts worst-case runner latency (boot + two scripted turns + PTY polling ≈ 10 s on fa-m5 minis), and the aged-row wait binds to the painted screen (`waitForScreen`) instead of the raw byte stream.

### Key decisions
- **No product change** — `lib/`, `bin/` and `test/` are byte-identical between `main` and `ai/gh-869` (only `flutter_app/`+`packages/fa_ui` differ, unused by the CLI), so a product regression was impossible; the A/B conclusion in the ticket was a test-timing race, not a composer/status-row bug.
- Reproduced the exact CI signature (`Expected: an object with length of <1> / Actual: []` at line 223, frame showing `┌─ Background jobs (5) · 0 running · 5 done · 0 lost`) by compressing the settle window: the whole bucket legitimately settled and drained before the capture — freeze + drain-once behaved correctly.
- Kept the ~1 s settle stagger the between-settles freeze assertion requires; `_firstSettle`/`_settledCardBody` timeouts raised 30 s → 60 s to absorb slow-runner render/persist lag past the longer sleeps.
- To un-block #899: merge `ai/gh-937` (or cherry-pick `2a70f077`) into `ai/gh-869`, then re-dispatch CI. #899 must not be admin-merged before that.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test --tags integration test/integration/job_board_stability_pty_test.dart
```
Both tests pass (was: deterministic failure of the 80/120/200 stacked-boards case on slow runners); `dart test test/cli/shell_job_board_test.dart` 35/35 green; analyzer clean.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — laye…

The harness has `waitForScreen` — so it already existed (used elsewhere too). Let me check where `waitForScreen` is used across the test suite to verify the pattern's established usage, and check `waitForText` usage with the raw output caveat. The harness doc says: "Use this when the assertion contract is the SCREEN" — so the change from `waitForText` → `waitForScreen` for `_olderRow` aligns with the harness's guidance.

Now let me think about the timing analysis carefully — the core of this fix:

Timeline of the first scenario (per column width):
1. Boot: `waitForBoot()` — banner `[Model]` + settle.
2. Wave one turn: `sendText('run wave one')` + Enter. The scripted stream emits 'launching the first wave' text + 5 tool calls (sleep 21..25, background). Wait for `Background jobs (5)` on screen (60s timeout). Wait for `_replyOne` (60s). `waitForOutput(settleMs: 400)`.
3. Wave two turn: `sendText('run wave two')` + Enter. Text + 6 tool calls (sleep 300, background). Wait for `_olderRow` via `waitForScreen` (60s). `waitForOutput(settleMs: 400)`. Capture `before`.
4. Freeze proof: `beforeOlder` must have exactly 1 row `· older` and `(5)`.
5. `waitForText(_firstSettle)` (60s) — first `exited(0)` at ~21s after wave-one job launch.
6. mid capture: `· older` row must equal `beforeOlder`.
7. `waitForText(_settledCardBody)` (60s) — full settle at ~25s.
8. after capture: aged row gone, exactly one settled card, wave two stays live.
9. `/exit`, wait exit code.

Total wall time per iteration: boot (~2-10s) + wave one (~2-5s) + wave two (~2-5s) + wait until first settle (the remaining of 21s since wave-one launch, minus elapsed) + up to 4s to last settle + settle buffers + exit. If boot+turns take ~10s, iteration ≈ 30-35s. Three iterations ≈ 100-105s, plus scenario B. Well within the 10-minute `@Timeout`.

Key race analysis:
- Old: sleeps 5..9s from wave-one launch. The `before` capture happens after wave-two's board row appears. On a slow runner, boot (~5s) + turn 1 (~3s) + turn 2 (~2s) + turn 3 (~3s) ≈ 13s > 9s — the entire wave-one bucket could be fully settled and drained by the time `before` is captured. Then `beforeOlder` is empty → `Expected: an object with length of <1> / Actual: []`. Matches the CI signature exactly. New: base 20 → settles at 21..25s, comfortably after the ~10s worst-case capture. Margin ~11s+. 

- Is 21..25s enough margin? Worst-case runner latency claim: boot + two scripted turns + PTY polling ≈ 10 s on fa-m5 minis. The `before` capture requires wave-two board row painted; if boot+3 turns took >21s, the capture would again miss. But the PR description says ~10s worst observed; 21 gives ~2x margin. Reasonable.

- One subtle thing: `_firstSettle` timeout raised 30→60s: the first settle lands at ~21s after wave-one launch; at the `waitForText(_firstSettle)` call, maybe ~10-15s have elapsed, so remaining ~6-11s normally; 30s would be plenty. But on a very slow runner, boot+turns could take longer... the deadline starts at the wait call; the settle happens 21s after launch regardless. If boot+turns took 15s, remaining wait = 6s. 30s was fine; 60s just absorbs extreme lag where the first settle could fire... hmm, actually the wait can't exceed ~21s after wave-one launch. If boot+turns took <21s, remaining wait <21s. If boot+turns took >21s, the bucket is already drained before `before` capture → the earlier `beforeOlder` assertion fails first. So the 30→60s raise is defensive, harmless.

- `_settledCardBody` timeout 30→60s: full settle at ~25s after launch; call happens at ~21s; remaining ~4s normally; if the runner is slow (say 15s to capture), remaining 10s. 30s was probably fine, 60s defensive. Harmless.

Potential concerns to flag in review:

1. **Test duration/timeout budget**: sleeps raised 5..9 → 21..25 nearly doubles per-iteration wall time (~+16s × 3 widths ≈ +48s). With the 10-minute file `@Timeout`, still fine. But CI job timeouts at the workflow level? Let me check how integration tests run in CI — the `--tags integration` suite. If there's a per-shard timeout, +48s could matter. Let me check `.github/workflows`.

2. **`waitForScreen` vs raw-text for `_olderRow`**: The regex `r'Background jobs \(5\) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older'` — in `screenText`, lines are joined and trimmed of empty lines. `waitForScreen` checks `screen.contains(pattern)`. The viewport line may have the `· older` suffix... the row is painted as one line if wide enough; at 80 columns, could `Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older` wrap or elide? The row is the collapsed board summary row. At 80 columns: "┌─ Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older …" — hmm, that's ~60+ chars plus border. `┌─ ` (3) + text (~55) + maybe more. The test previously used `waitForText` with the same regex and passed on main (the ticket says main is green on this file, and this exact test at 80 cols passed — the failing case was the timing race, not the match). So the row fits at 80 cols. OK.

      - name: Self-hosted toolcache redirect (fa-m5)

# Changelog

## 1.0.472


- fix(env): `LocalExecutionEnv` forwards `renamePath` — kernel-mode cube
  exec was dead since #803's atomic profile restage (the
  `RenamableFileSystem` capability probe failed at the base env), making
  every kernel-backend bash call fail with "profile staging failed" and
  keeping the macOS nested-rw integration gate red on darwin dev
  machines. Capability restored + unit regression; the full
  `fa_cube_integration_test` suite is green again through real
  sandbox-exec.
- fix(781): green the nightly, nightly parity at PR time. Five
  `cli_visual` regressions red on main for days are fixed at the test
  layer — the product behavior was already correct in each case:
  sandbox-HOME (`#508`) can never have a working keychain so `key set`
  honestly reports `could not save`; the `/agents` hub overlay
  (`#316`) never carried the picker's `mail:N` cue (hub rows now
  append ` · mail:N` via a re-entrancy-guarded fabric peek, refresh-only
  re-push can never force the overlay open); the secret-sheet rename hint
  copy changed in `#627`; the markdown-table and sibling tests shared one
  fixed port whose leak cascaded into an unreadable `SocketException`
  (ephemeral ports now); the seeded-fleet fixture lied about liveness
  (a seeded `running` row is zombie-settled to `failed` at boot, `#332`,
  which reordered the tree under arrow navigation — seed `idle`).
  `bin/fah.dart` lost a duplicated remote-catalog preload (merge artifact
  from `#411`+`#448`) that double-awaited boot latency up to +10s
  offline. CI: the two nightly-only legs — PTY/CLI integration + CLI
  coverage ratchet and the Terminal-visual PTY suite — now run on every
  PR (aggregate Quality gate, same secret shape as the nightly/gardener
  so the ratchet measures the same surface; `#781`).

## 1.0.468


- feat(tui): the omp status bar engine (#805). **Behavior note**: the
  `tui:` config section is now parsed strictly — an unknown key under
  `tui:` (e.g. a typo'd `theme2:` left behind by hand-editing) throws
  `ConfigException` at boot instead of being silently ignored. Remove

## PR Description

### What changed
Fixed the deterministic `job_board_stability_pty_test` red on PR #899 (ai/gh-869): the freeze-proof's `before` capture now has a settle window (wave-one sleeps 21..25 s, was 5..9 s) that outlasts worst-case runner latency (boot + two scripted turns + PTY polling ≈ 10 s on fa-m5 minis), and the aged-row wait binds to the painted screen (`waitForScreen`) instead of the raw byte stream.

### Key decisions
- **No product change** — `lib/`, `bin/` and `test/` are byte-identical between `main` and `ai/gh-869` (only `flutter_app/`+`packages/fa_ui` differ, unused by the CLI), so a product regression was impossible; the A/B conclusion in the ticket was a test-timing race, not a composer/status-row bug.
- Reproduced the exact CI signature (`Expected: an object with length of <1> / Actual: []` at line 223, frame showing `┌─ Background jobs (5) · 0 running · 5 done · 0 lost`) by compressing the settle window: the whole bucket legitimately settled and drained before the capture — freeze + drain-once behaved correctly.
- Kept the ~1 s settle stagger the between-settles freeze assertion requires; `_firstSettle`/`_settledCardBody` timeouts raised 30 s → 60 s to absorb slow-runner render/persist lag past the longer sleeps.
- To un-block #899: merge `ai/gh-937` (or cherry-pick `2a70f077`) into `ai/gh-869`, then re-dispatch CI. #899 must not be admin-merged before that.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test --tags integration test/integration/job_board_stability_pty_test.dart
```
Both tests pass (was: deterministic failure of the 80/120/200 stacked-boards case on slow runners); `dart test test/cli/shell_job_board_test.dart` 35/35 green; analyzer clean.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the

Now let me think about the timing analysis carefully — the core of this fix:

Timeline of the first scenario (per column width):
1. Boot: `waitForBoot()` — banner `[Model]` + settle.
2. Wave one turn: `sendText('run wave one')` + Enter. The scripted stream emits 'launching the first wave' text + 5 tool calls (sleep 21..25, background). Wait for `Background jobs (5)` on screen (60s timeout). Wait for `_replyOne` (60s). `waitForOutput(settleMs: 400)`.
3. Wave two turn: `sendText('run wave two')` + Enter. Text + 6 tool calls (sleep 300, background). Wait for `_olderRow` via `waitForScreen` (60s). `waitForOutput(settleMs: 400)`. Capture `before`.
4. Freeze proof: `beforeOlder` must have exactly 1 row `· older` and `(5)`.
5. `waitForText(_firstSettle)` (60s) — first `exited(0)` at ~21s after wave-one job launch.
6. mid capture: `· older` row must equal `beforeOlder`.
7. `waitForText(_settledCardBody)` (60s) — full settle at ~25s.
8. after capture: aged row gone, exactly one settled card, wave two stays live.
9. `/exit`, wait exit code.

Total wall time per iteration: boot (~2-10s) + wave one (~2-5s) + wave two (~2-5s) + wait until first settle (the remaining of 21s since wave-one launch, minus elapsed) + up to 4s to last settle + settle buffers + exit. If boot+turns take ~10s, iteration ≈ 30-35s. Three iterations ≈ 100-105s, plus scenario B. Well within the 10-minute `@Timeout`.

Key race analysis:
- Old: sleeps 5..9s from wave-one launch. The `before` capture happens after wave-two's board row appears. On a slow runner, boot (~5s) + turn 1 (~3s) + turn 2 (~2s) + turn 3 (~3s) ≈ 13s > 9s — the entire wave-one bucket could be fully settled and drained by the time `before` is captured. Then `beforeOlder` is empty → `Expected: an object with length of <1> / Actual: []`. Matches the CI signature exactly. New: base 20 → settles at 21..25s, comfortably after the ~10s worst-case capture. Margin ~11s+. 

- Is 21..25s enough margin? Worst-case runner latency claim: boot + two scripted turns + PTY polling ≈ 10 s on fa-m5 minis. The `before` capture requires wave-two board row painted; if boot+3 turns took >21s, the capture would again miss. But the PR description says ~10s worst observed; 21 gives ~2x margin. Reasonable.

- One subtle thing: `_firstSettle` timeout raised 30→60s: the first settle lands at ~21s after wave-one launch; at the `waitForText(_firstSettle)` call, maybe ~10-15s have elapsed, so remaining ~6-11s normally; 30s would be plenty. But on a very slow runner, boot+turns could take longer... the deadline starts at the wait call; the settle happens 21s after launch regardless. If boot+turns took 15s, remaining wait = 6s. 30s was fine; 60s just absorbs extreme lag where the first settle could fire... hmm, actually the wait can't exceed ~21s after wave-one launch. If boot+turns took <21s, remaining wait <21s. If boot+turns took >21s, the bucket is already drained before `before` capture → the earlier `beforeOlder` assertion fails first. So the 30→60s raise is defensive, harmless.

- `_settledCardBody` timeout 30→60s: full settle at ~25s after launch; call happens at ~21s; remaining ~4s normally; if the runner is slow (say 15s to capture), remaining 10s. 30s was probably fine, 60s defensive. Harmless.

Potential concerns to flag in review:

1. **Test duration/timeout budget**: sleeps raised 5..9 → 21..25 nearly doubles per-iteration wall time (~+16s × 3 widths ≈ +48s). With the 10-minute file `@Timeout`, still fine. But CI job timeouts at the workflow level? Let me check how integration tests run in CI — the `--tags integration` suite. If there's a per-shard timeout, +48s could matter. Let me check `.github/workflows`.

So the row fits at 80 cols. OK.

      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
      # Self-hosted fa-m5 minis have no /Users/runner home — setup-* would
      # try to mkdir the hosted toolcache and die. Redirect it to a stable
      # per-runner path (warm across runs); hosted runners are untouched.
      - name: Self-hosted toolcache redirect (fa-m5)
        if: startsWith(runner.name, 'fa-m5')

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1

      # consumer here is the pure-python coverage ratchet below — system
      # python3 (CLT on macOS, preinstalled on hosted images) suffices.
      - name: python3 available
        run: python3 --version
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: dart test --tags integration (excluding browser-ext)
        run: >-

          --coverage=coverage
      - name: Format coverage to lcov

      - name: CLI coverage ratchet (lib/src/cli/**, baseline only up)

The integration leg (`dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext --coverage=coverage`) has a 60-minute job timeout (line 500's `timeout-minutes: 60` corresponds to the job containing line 550). Adding ~30-50s to one file within a 60-minute leg is negligible. The file-level `@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 10))` comfortably absorbs the +30-50s.

Now, let me validate the test compiles and analyzer is clean, and quickly run the non-PTY unit test the PR description references (`test/cli/shell_job_board_test.dart`, 35 tests) as sanity. Also try to run the changed integration test? It's a real PTY test, spawning the CLI with scripted streams; it could take ~2-3 min. It would be strong verification. The environment is a Linux runner with dart available? Let me check `dart --version`. The repo has pubspec; tests may need `dart pub get`. Let me try analyzer first.

Also, let me double check one potential correctness subtlety: at 80 columns, does the frozen row fit so `waitForScreen` can match `Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older` as one screen line? screenLines drops empty lines and keeps others; contains() on the joined text — if the row wrapped into two lines, the joined string would contain a `\n` in the middle → no match → 60s timeout → flaky. But: main is green with `waitForText` which ALSO checks screenText (`output.contains(pattern) || screenText.contains(pattern)`) — and the row appears in the failing CI frame as a single line `┌─ Background jobs (5) · 0 running · 5 done · 0 lost`. The full string with `· 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older`: "Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older" is 57 chars; plus "┌─ " prefix = 60 chars; fits 80 cols. The `_olderRow` regex is matched against screenText (which joins lines with \n) — fits one line. OK.

Another subtlety: `viewportLines` at 80x24 — `Terminal(maxLines: rows * 4)`. Fine.

One more: the PR bumps `_firstSettle`/`_settledCardBody` timeouts 30→60s "to absorb slow-runner render/persist lag past the longer sleeps". Since the file has @Timeout(10 min), a hung wait would still terminate. Fine.

Now, is there any ISSUE with the increase? Let me think about the whole-suite duration math precisely.

Per width iteration:
- boot: waitForBoot (up to 90s timeout; typical 2-8s)
- wave one turn: ~1-3s (scripted, instant)
- wait `Background jobs (5)`: instant-ish after board paints
- wait `_replyOne`: turn 2 scripted, ~1s
- settle 400ms
- wave two turn: ~1-3s
- waitForScreen(_olderRow): instant after wave-two board paints (~1-2s)
- settle 400ms
- capture `before` at T ≈ boot + ~6-10s
- wave-one jobs settle at 21-25s after their launch (which happened during turn 1, ~2-4s after boot). So first settle at wall ~23-29s; wait for it ≈ 13-19s.
- mid capture, then wait full settle (last at ~25s after launch → ~29s wall; ~2-8s more).
- `after` capture, assertions, `/exit` + exit-code wait (15s cap).

So per iteration ≈ 35-45s (vs ~20-25s before) → +~50s total across 3 widths. Test 2 (restart) also launches wave one with the longer sleeps, but kills before settle; duration unchanged (~boot + a few seconds).

Everything fits: file timeout 10 min; CI leg 60 min. Good.

Now the deeper review question — does this fix actually address the root cause robustly, or just widen the race window? The failure was: whole bucket settled+drained before `before` capture → `beforeOlder` empty. The fix: (a) push the settle window 2.3x further out (21..25s vs worst ~10s capture latency), and (b) gate the capture on the screen showing the frozen all-running row (`waitForScreen(_olderRow)` — `5 running · 0 done`), so if the bucket did drain early, the test now fails with a 60s timeout naming the pattern + screen dump (a diagnosable failure), not a confusing empty-list assertion. Combined, this converts both the likely case (never happens with 2x margin) and the residual case (clear diagnostic) into better states. That's a sound mitigation for a test-only flake.

Residual nit: the ~2x margin is empirical ("~10 s worst on fa-m5-class runners"), not enforced — a runner 2x slower than the observed worst would reintroduce the empty-capture failure, but now with the timeout diagnostic (b). Acceptable; could note as SUGGESTION-level: consider making the margin structural, e.g., waiting for the first wave-one settle to be IMMINENT before capturing... actually you can't easily assert "not yet settled" other than what waitForScreen(_olderRow) already does (the frozen row only exists while the newer bucket is live AND prints all-running counts — hmm, actually the frozen row is printed at aging time with then-current counts; if the bucket ages at `5 running · 0 done` the row is exactly `_olderRow`. waitForScreen returns as soon as that row is painted. A wave-one job can't settle before aging unless latency > 21s. So (b) already structuralizes the capture: the capture happens strictly before any settle, unless the 21s window is exceeded, in which case timeout — not a false pass. That IS the structural fix; the base=20 just needs to stay above realistic latency. Good.)

One more consideration — false-pass risk introduced by waitForScreen for `_olderRow`: previously waitForText matched raw OR screen. Raw matching could fire on the row's raw bytes before painted... now screen-only, strictly stronger. No false-pass introduced.

What about `_firstSettle = 'exited(0)'` — `waitForText` matches raw OR screen. The raw stream includes the settle notice printed by the CLI (`[bash] sh-… exited(0)`). This is a transcript notice — fine. But could 'exited(0)' appear EARLY from something else? The `/exit` command? No — that's later. Wave-two jobs sleep 300s. OK, unchanged behavior anyway.

Now check: are there other tests/files that copy the same wave pattern with 4+i sleeps that would also need the fix? The ticket is specific to this test. Quick grep for 'p539-wave1' or 'sleep ${4' to check duplication.

Also verify the claim "Both tests pass" — I'll try to run the changed integration test if the environment allows (needs dart + pub get + pty + bash `sleep`). It runs `dart bin/fah.dart`... spawns real CLI with FA_TEST_STREAM_SCRIPT. Should work on Linux runner. Time: ~2-4 min. Worth it for a high-confidence review. But careful: it writes to /tmp/fa_539_home and /tmp/fa_539_proj (shared fixed paths) — fine solo.

  sandbox-exec.

  `cli_visual` regressions red on main for days are fixed at the test

  honestly reports `could not save`; the `/agents` hub overlay

  copy changed in `#627`; the markdown-table and sibling tests shared one
  fixed port whose leak cascaded into an unreadable `SocketException`

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — laye…

3. Changed `harness.waitForText(_olderRow, ...)` to `harness.waitForScreen(_olderRow, ...)`.

- `waitForScreen` exists in `pty_harness.dart` and its semantics (does it match against the painted screen? what's the timeout behavior?).
- `waitForText` semantics.
- Whether the test's timing analysis is sound: the wave-one sleeps now 21..25s. The freeze proof's `before` capture happens after wave two is launched. Timing: boot + turn 1 (launch wave one) + turn 2 (reply) + turn 3 (launch wave two) + turn 4 (reply). Wave one jobs start at turn 1; they settle at start+21..25s. The `before` capture happens shortly after wave two's board row is painted. If boot+turns takes ~10s worst case, then the `before` capture is at ~10-12s, while jobs settle at 21..25s — leaving ~10s margin. That's the claim in the PR.

But wait — is there a subtlety? The `beforeOlder` assertion expects exactly ONE row containing '· older' and '(5)'. With sleeps 21..25, at `before` capture time all 5 jobs are still running (5 running · 0 done), so the board shows `Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older`. Good.

However — hold on. There's a potential problem: the freeze proof comment says "wave one's jobs settle under the camera (sleeps 21..25 s)". The first settle is at base+1=21s after launch. Then `waitForText(_firstSettle)` — first settle notice. Then mid capture: `· older` row must be byte-identical. After the first settle (4 jobs still live), the frozen row stays `5 running · 0 done`. OK.

Then "Full settle hands the bucket to the transcript": waits for `_settledCardBody` ('bash_job status lists ids'). The last job settles at 25s. OK.

But there's another important consideration: each of the three column widths (80/120/200) re-runs the whole scenario with a fresh session. So the test now takes 3 × ~25-30s = ~75-90s+ boot overhead per width. The `@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 10))` — 10 minutes total for the file. Each iteration: boot (~2-5s?), wave one launch, wave two launch, wait for settle (~25s from job launch), full settle... plus `/exit`. With 21..25s sleeps, each iteration takes roughly 30-40s including boot and overhead. Three iterations ≈ 100-120s. Plus test 2 (restart-lost REG). Should fit in 10 min. Previously with 5..9s sleeps, iterations were faster (~15-25s each).

Now let me think about the timing analysis carefully — the core of this fix:

Timeline of the first scenario (per column width):
1. Boot: `waitForBoot()` — banner `[Model]` + settle.
2. Wave one turn: `sendText('run wave one')` + Enter. The scripted stream emits 'launching the first wave' text + 5 tool calls (sleep 21..25, background). Wait for `Background jobs (5)` on screen (60s timeout). Wait for `_replyOne` (60s). `waitForOutput(settleMs: 400)`.
3. Wave two turn: `sendText('run wave two')` + Enter. Text + 6 tool calls (sleep 300, background). Wait for `_olderRow` via `waitForScreen` (60s). `waitForOutput(settleMs: 400)`. Capture `before`.
4. Freeze proof: `beforeOlder` must have exactly 1 row `· older` and `(5)`.
5. `waitForText(_firstSettle)` (60s) — first `exited(0)` at ~21s after wave-one job launch.
6. mid capture: `· older` row must equal `beforeOlder`.
7. `waitForText(_settledCardBody)` (60s) — full settle at ~25s.

9. `/exit`, wait exit code.

Total wall time per iteration: boot (~2-10s) + wave one (~2-5s) + wave two (~2-5s) + wait until first settle (the remaining of 21s since wave-one launch, minus elapsed) + up to 4s to last settle + settle buffers + exit. Key race analysis:
- Old: sleeps 5..9s from wave-one launch. The `before` capture happens after wave-two's board row appears. # self-skip those legs gracefully; the gate stays honest either way.

      # number and would pass while the nightly fails. Missing keys (forks)
      # self-skip those legs gracefully; the gate stays honest either way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
      # Self-hosted fa-m5 minis have no /Users/runner home — setup-* would
      # try to mkdir the hosted toolcache and die. Redirect it to a stable
      # per-runner path (warm across runs); hosted runners are untouched.
      - name: Self-hosted toolcache redirect (fa-m5)
        if: startsWith(runner.name, 'fa-m5')
        run: echo "RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE=${{ runner.workspace }}/toolcache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # setup-python hardcodes AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY=/Users/runner/hostedtoolcache
      # on every macOS runner (hosted layout assumption) and overwrites
      # RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE, so on self-hosted macs without a 'runner' user it
      # dies with "mkdir: /Users/runner: Permission denied". The only python
      # consumer here is the pure-python coverage ratchet below — system
      # python3 (CLT on macOS, preinstalled on hosted images) suffices.
      - name: python3 available
        run: python3 --version
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: dart test --tags integration (excluding browser-ext)
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
          --coverage=coverage
      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
      - name: CLI coverage ratchet (lib/src/cli/**, baseline only up)
